title: King Oliver as a leader and his enormous appetite
summary: Howard calls Oliver businesslike and comical, easy to work for, and describes his huge meals and home life.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: How'd you dress with Oliver's band? Tuxedo. Every night, tuxedo. That's right. What kind of a leader was Oliver? How was he?

No trouble whatsoever. Yeah. A lot of foolishness. I mean, he was strictly business on the job, but he was comical, you know, do things, make you laugh. I had no trouble with a very fine guy to work with.
We all enjoyed working with each other, no kidding. We sure did.
He was a very big eater, is that true?
Cut the thing off. I'm going to tell him something. Tell me that.
Oh really, could he accomplishes you?
Oh heck yes. Street times as much as me. I'm not a big eater anymore. I'm talking how you were in those days.
Well you asked me a question.

Was he the big, you mean as I was then? Yeah. Oh yes. His wife used to give him a great big bowl full of coffee. You know, no such thing as a coffee cup. And big plates of rice, you know, almost like a casserole. Oh yes, he had an enormous appetite. What was like one typical dinner like? What did he eat? Oh he ate mostly at home.
Oh yeah, he ate at home. Oh sure. Was his wife in Chicago with him? Yes. That's right. Did they have a house or an apartment? I had an apartment.
Did you eat with him much? Hmm? Did you eat with him much?
Do they have any children? One. I do. Yeah, she's dead now too. I do. I do. I do. I do. I do. I do.
